items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: So we decided that the best way to title the group was the Montgomery-Johnsons... The tenor player, Pookie, was just a great player. He and Wes, the front line, played so well together

ctx.x: No. The customers could come back and talk to us, but we couldn't go out there and set with them. We wasn't allowed to sit in the room. That was just a way of life. I didn't pay it too much attention 'til I had gone and come back, and I said, 'Wait, I can't come through there. What am I doing

coming through the back door?' I wasn't voluntarily coming back there, looking for more of the same. I was passing through. So they said, 'With this thing happening, you will be...' They had blown it up, which was good for Indianapolis, and they wanted the Montgomery Brothers out there. It so happens that to make the quintet up, there was a tenor player by the name of Pookie Johnson and a drummer by the name of Sonny Johnson.
